Backyard Ballistics This forum is dedicated to the safe teaching and responsible handling of high and low explosives. You will not find any information on how to make "bombs" or any such device(s) . Backyard ballistics will teach you the science and the art of pyrotechnics and how to manufacture and use explosives/pyrotechnics safely and responsibly. Backyard ballistics is also a haven for rocketry and pneumatic cannons. All information contained within this forum is for educational purposes ONLY. My girlfriend was coming round and she was asking for ages to see some HEs

So



I put my polycarbonate garden table (with a 10mm by 30mm slit cut in it, so i can see) 5m away from the bucket which i filled with a dead rat my mother wanted buried and high density earth, I then proceeded to hide behind it with goggles, detting system and ear protection on (while girlfriend was ~30m away in a house)I flicked the switch and all went well except I was a tad bit close and got hit in the face with a tiny bit of earth...but here comes the funny part the window the the girlfriend was viewing from a (big one) had now been smeared with the rats guts and made a whole big blood splatter.

oh and in case your wondering the rat was placed on top of the charge to seal it...

Spatula Tzar
Regular
  
Re: Pyro Related Random Thread ( PRRT ) #27
It's not so much the resistance as the wattage.

12V * .7A = 8.4 Watts

To reduce the voltage to adjust the speed, much of this power is burned up in the resistor. To prevent fires and overheating, you must use a potentiometer rated to at least the maximum current draw of the motor. I'd find a 10 Watt one.

Larger potentiometers are often called rheostats, and can be found fairly cheaply as dimmer controls for lights.

As for resistance, a higher rating will give you more precise control, but pretty much all of them will give you a 0-max speed control on the motor.

Wire it in series. Parallel might look better for low wattage potentiometers, but series prevents it from creating a dead short accross the power terminals (a bad thing.)

Of course, burning up excess power is a terribly inneficient method. There are plenty of better speed control circuits out there if you care.

Resistance increases with wire distance, especially noticable with thin 26 AWG telephone wire. Use 18 gauge. If you're cheap, use two or three strands of telephone wire in parallel to create essentially one thicker wire.

What do you mean by the primary composition? What is it supposed to ignite? KMnO4 + S might not seem very sensetive, but some sulfur mixes become unstable over time.

The flare is essentially a rocket, so model the launcher after an RPG. Have a large diameter pipe with plenty of airspace for the barrel, so it won't break if the flare explodes.

Definately go for electrical ignition.

quote:Originally posted by Modzilla:

Totaljackass:

You could, if I am not very much mistaken, use a bigger battery OR stick a capacitor before the wire. Therefore when you flick the switch more current is going through. So Resistance is less of a problem.

You are very much mistaken. A capacitor will not counteract resistance, it will merely allow current flow until the capacitor is filled, then stop it. Either use a higher voltage (two or more batteries in series), use thicker wire, or use four stands of telephone wire in parallel instead of two.

Here's an organic peroxide puzzle for you:

I tried my first synth of MEKP, but I forgot to freeze the H2O2. When I added salt water, I could see some oily drops and swirls on the top, but no definite layer. Not wanting to toss it out just yet, I let it sit for a few weeks.

I come back and see a thin crystal lattice 1-2 cm in diameter floating on top. I poked it, and it sunk, where there were a bunch of other transparent crystals. Extracting a few, I did a burn test, and it behaved just like AP. Note that the crystals had the consistency of sugar-water slurry, despite being completely dry.

What is this? A solid version of MEKP? I'll do a hammer test next.

H2O2 decomposition is a catalyic reaction; that is, even with one molecule of MnO2, you could decompose as much H2O2 as you wanted, given enough time. I think silver also acts as a catalyst on H2O2; they actually hgave rockets that work by shooting 90% H2O2 through a silver mesh.

EDIT: and its a real slick way to produce oxygen.

Urea.

If you do it on a lower heat it will generally come over in a higher concentration with less NO2. Much slower, but as long as you can have the stove at one setting and just leave it, its not really something that needs to be constantly watched. If the stove was on the lowest heat, you could raise the flask higher away from the flame. I have to do that with my hot-plate because it essentially turns on and off to maintain an average temp, i set it so it is constantly on and just raise my retort a little higher because the hot-plate gets too hot and it will boil it to fast for my liking.

Its not really an issue with your setup, but if you put an aluminum foil shield between your heat source and ice-water cooled collection flask it helps a lot.

Nice improvised setup though!

Yes the buffers in liquid lightning suck for nitrations. I've experimented with them and adding a small amount of H2O2 at 30% will oxidize the buffers and make the solution completely clear. This can be reconcentrated

Also distillation is a possibility with the right equipment. A last possibility is heating it at boiling and refluxing to break down the buffers and pour the cooled acid through an activated charcoal filter however on second thought that might oxidize the carbon...

The first thing I mentioned is definatley worth a try if you have the supplies.

I found the answer to the CuCl2 problem: H2O2. A mix of H2O2 and HCl first ionizes the copper, then the ion reacts with the chlorine cations. The process is very similar to aqua regia.

http://antoine.frostburg.edu/chem/senese/101/redox/faq/h2o2-cu.shtml

The second way is simply electrolysis with copper electrodes in a sodium chloride solution.

quote:Originally posted by Pyrology:

Sentinel, what did you do differently in your new batch?



Well first of all I used my magnetic stirrer, so it was constantly being stirred. Secondly, I added the AN to my H2SO4 when they were both at room temp; I did some of it in an ice bath during the first batch. I also cut the cellulose into tiny shreds with scissors, although I'm not sure if this made a huge effect. Most importaintly, I let it nitrate for an hour and a half before crashing/neutralizing. I let it dry for two days before testing.

EDIT: by comparing the remains of carbonized cellulose left from when the finished NC burned, I figure that I should let my next batch nitrate for 2 or maybe eiven 3 hours. The residue left from the better batch was considerably less than the slower-burning batch; this leads me to believe that more cellulose was nitrated, but residue still means incomplete nitration.

Re: Pyro Related Random Thread ( PRRT ) #27
quote:"A makeshift fume hood is really easy to build. If you have some acrylic sheet lying around, make a box out of it. If you can, make it a kind of rounded shape with a sloping chimney up to the exaust. This prevents the fresh air from making a straight line from the intake to the exaust. Hook some dryer vent pipe (the metal-looking stuff that colapses and bends), and run that to the wall. Since you said that you already had a fan, put the pipe up to the fan and see if it will suck in. You should be able to feel the air flow at the mouth of the hood. If that doesn't work, a vacume cleaner motor has plenty of pull for even a larger hood. I got one at a garage sale for .50$. You should have a front that you can stick on it with just a few air holes in case something starts to react really bad. If you can amke a sliding sash (the door is called a sash for some reason)."

Ok, sounds exactly like what we were going to do. May I ask how I could construct - or buy - a fan for this? Today, we went through a hardware store and they had no duct fans that would work well. I am thinking about just using a computer case fan, but then again, it would require a power supply...

" Procedure

Materials:

Sulfuric acid conc. (H2SO4)

Potassium nitrate (KNO3)

or sodium nitrate (NaNO3)

or calcium nitrate (Ca(NO3)2)

When making nitric acid you gotta have right equipment, or else it will be dangerous and messy. Set up equipment for basic distillation, all equipment must be made of glass or other inert material (for example teflon).

Place any nitrate salt (for example KNO3) in distilling vessel, add enough sulfuric acid (H2SO4) to cover the salt. Heat reaction mixture to 100oC and then, gradually, to 120oC. Warning, this should be made in good ventilated area (reaction will produce some NOx gases).

Reaction is considered complete when reaction mixture becomes slightly yellow and nitric acid stops condensing. "

Re: Pyro Related Random Thread ( PRRT ) #27
Nitrite + HCl should fizzle and produce nitrogen oxides, while nitrate probably wont fizz much if at all immediatly.

HNO2 = Nitrous acid

HNO3 = Nitric acid

They do NOT add the same group to a substance.

So yes, some of the left over from smoke mix or BP is KNO2, but there is also other substances like K2O, C, K2CO3 mabey, etc... Not too hard to seperate though. Probably not much KNO2, though if i had known this from when i first started making smoke mix, i would have definately saved all the left over material to extract, im sure i would have had atleast around 200g of KNO2 by now.

Re: Pyro Related Random Thread ( PRRT ) #27
Flour and many other carbohydrates become explosive when they are hanging in the air as dust. It only takes 1 or 2 grams of dust per cubic foot of air (50 or so grams per cubic meter) for the mixture to be ignitable. Flour grains are so tiny that they burn instantly. When one grain burns, it lights other grains near it, and the flame front can flash through a dust cloud with explosive force. Just about any carbohydrate dust, including sugar, pudding mix, fine sawdust, etc., will explode once ignited.

When you hear about an explosion in a grain elevator on the news, this is what has occurred. A spark or a source of heat ignited the dust in the air and it exploded.

Re: Pyro Related Random Thread ( PRRT ) #27
I drew up a few sketches of a classic plunger box. (http://img352.imageshack.us/img352/2878/plunger8xm.png)

In the first one, the plunger has two sheathes attatched, which slide over the two greased rods inside the box. The two switches to on the sides serve as redundent safeties, being wired in series with the main switch on the bottom. Dual springs act as a bumper.

In the second sketch, the plunger handle consists of a pipe which slides over a single greased rod. This is simpler, but the handle can spin on its axis.

I also drew up the circuit (http://img352.imageshack.us/img352/453/circuit5zt.png) I use for my igniters. The two arrows connect to the igniter. When the DPST switch is closed, an LED lights, indicating the device is armed. When the igniter is properly connected, a second LED lights letting you know it is ready to be fired. The momentary switch diverts the full power of the batery to the igniter, firing it.

Asilentbob, here's something. Its a peroxide but seems interesting.

10) Tetramethylenediperoxidedicarbamide (T.M.D.D.)



This is a similar explosive peroxide to Hexamethylenetriperoxidediamine (H.M.T.D.)This procedure came from a Swedish text which I had to translate. Before I saw the text, I had never seen another Swedish word, so I can't gurantee 100% accuracy of this translation. I have not yet tried it as I have no formaldehyde right now. I think that the molecule will be less stressed than that of H.M.T.D., resulting in a more stable product, but I'm not sure...



You will need:



16mL of 35% formaldehyde solution,

22mL of 35% hydrogen peroxide (or equivalent),

6g of urea,

10mL of 50% sulphuric acid,

An ice bath,

A fridge,

500mL of distilled water,

250mL of 10% sodium carbonate solution,

(Acetone?),

A thermometer,

A 150mL beaker,

A pipette,

A filter funnel,

A filter paper.



1) Mix the formaldehyde and the hydrogen peroxide in the 150mL beaker, and dissolve the urea in it.

2) Cool it to 5*C in the ice bath, and add the sulphuric acid drop by drop, while stirring with the thermometer and no letting the temperature go above 20*C.

3) After the addition of the acid, put the 150mL beaker of reactants into the fridge for 48 hours.

4) After this time, filter out the crystals of T.M.D.D.

5) While they're in the filter paper, wash the crystals with 100mL of water, then with the 250mL of sodium carbonate solution, then with the remaining 400mL of water.

6) I think the Swedish text said to recrystalise from acetone. So try this, but if it doesn't work then just dry the crystals in a cool, dry place!



Apparently this explosive is really bad, and can even be easily dead-pressed! That's unusual for an organic peroxide explosive, eh?

copied from here http://www.flashbangboom.homestead.com/procedures.html

...After google, wiki, etc...

You could do it with CO2 and H2:

"CO + 2H2 = CH3OH

CO2 + 3H2 = CH3OH + H2O"

Pyrolysis of wood and a bunch of distillations perhaps.

Re: Pyro Related Random Thread ( PRRT ) #27
I did some tests with AP putty. I mixed AP with three different plastics: NC, polystyrene, and acrylic. Each were mixed 1:1 by weight and dissolved in acetone. The glop was then drawn up into a vinyl tube and dried.

I've used NC before, so it will be my control group. It dries into a fairly thin layer inside the tube. When lit, it jumped a short distance like a rocket, then exploded.

The polystyrene is crap. It burns incredibly slowly, and the tiniest pop of AP extinguishes it.

Acrylic works well. It dries much more solid than NC, so it seems better suited. It made a nice sharp bang like NC.

2006-01-26, 02:39
totaljackass
Regular
  
Re: Pyro Related Random Thread ( PRRT ) #27
Either distill it or maybe freezing to a very low temperature will reduce solubility and can be filtered. But good luck filtering. Conc. HNO3 will eat almost ANYTHING. That means it might be hard to do with cofee filters ect. Although I did have plastic particles in my HNO3 that came off a disolved rubber stopper on my still which I filtered through coffee filters. But it was a small amount and the filter barely survived. The sulfate is ok though. Lowers yields in some synths, but most synths you add excess H2SO4 for a catalyst, so the mix is fine. But its better to prepare right before the synth. Many synths need different amounts and catalyst HNO3 ratios. But keep that stuff and distill it. It would be a good enough grade for RDX if distilled right.
